title: The Company's survey marks the Hale cutting
summary: A' Chompanaidh's surveyors, working out a new gallery above Baile dhìreach, mark the narrow customary cutting held by Eilidh nic Ruairidh's line for four generations. The agent Pryce offers Thomas Hale a small sum to sign it over rather than test the Company's claim.

title: Thomas Hale's suit filed at Ros dhomhain
summary: Thomas Hale walks the three days from Baile dhìreach to Ros dhomhain and files a claim at the Company's court, a copy of his grandmother's marriage roll in his coat and no other paper. The clerk gives a hearing date a full season off, at the back of the court's list.

title: Mairead nic Amhlaidh copies the marriage roll
summary: The custodian of Baile dhìreach copies, under her own seal, the roll's page of the second year recording the marriage of Eilidh nic Ruairidh and Samuel Hale in two tongues, so that Thomas Hale may carry proof of the line to the Company's court.

title: Dunstan's ruling read at the Company's counter
summary: Oliver Dunstan's ruling against Thomas Hale is posted at the Ros dhomhain counter among a dozen others of the same list. It holds that no marriage entered in a custodian's roll, however old, creates a line the Administration recognises, and confirms the cutting to the Company.

title: The cutting at Seann Bhral taken
summary: A second magistrate at Ros dhomhain, citing Thomas Hale's case by name, decides a claim on a customary working at Seann Bhral against a cooper's daughter's line, married three generations back to a human pilot. The ruling runs to a single page.

title: Mairead nic Amhlaidh stops entering marriages in the roll
summary: The custodian of Baile dhìreach ceases to enter marriages between Dia-thìrich and humans in her roll, judging that under Dunstan's rule such an entry has become a paper a family's enemies may use against it rather than one that protects anything.

title: The coast's custodians follow Baile dhìreach's example
summary: Within the year other custodians of the western coast quietly stop entering two-tongue marriages in their own rolls, without any word agreed between the districts. The marriages go on; only the writing of them fails.

title: Griogair mac Ailein taken up at Cnoc chaol
summary: Griogair mac Ailein, a breaker of the Cnoc chaol sorting-floor, is taken up by the Company's constables over a dispute at the pay office and refuses to sign for a short-weighted cartload he did not cut. He is held in the Company's lock-up pending a hearing never set.

title: Griogair mac Ailein dies in the lock-up
summary: Griogair mac Ailein dies in the Company's lock-up at Cnoc chaol of a fever the Company's own surgeon records as already advanced when he was taken. He has no family living to claim him.

title: The fellowship at Baile thais buys the ground and the box
summary: The burial club newly begun among the pit crews of Baile thais and Cnoc chaol, calling itself the Lamp-Watch among its own members, gathers its members' wages to buy Griogair mac Ailein's grave-ground and coffin, meaning his burying to be seen done properly in the Company's own eye.

title: Thomas Hale sent for to read the surgeon's note
summary: Dòmhnall Ruadh, a crew-leader of Baile thais, carries a letter to Baile dhìreach asking Thomas Hale, known along the coast for his hard-won knowledge of the Administration's law, to stand at Griogair mac Ailein's graveside and read the Company surgeon's note releasing the body.

title: Thomas Hale reads the surgeon's note at the grave
summary: At a grave dug on the bare hill above the Cnoc chaol pit-head, Thomas Hale reads Griogair mac Ailein's release aloud in the Company's own tongue before some thirty of the fellowship, so that no clerk may afterward say the burying was done without the Company's leave.
